#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH --nodes=7
#SBATCH --time=05:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=dask_cluster
#SBATCH --ntasks=7
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=36

# This is a 1-to-1 conversion of a slurm script.
# The following corrections have been made to the original script:
# - Replaced non-standard '$CPUS_ON_NODE' with the correct Slurm variable '$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE'.
# - Corrected hard-coded path '/home/rjackson/scheduler.json' to use the '$HOME' variable for portability.

# Environment variables
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE
export MPLBACKEND="agg"
export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8
export LANG=en_US.UTF-8
 
# Write ~/scheduler.json file in home directory
# connect with
# >>> from dask.distributed import Client
# >>> client = Client(scheduler_file='~/scheduler.json')

# Start scheduler on one task, and workers on the remaining tasks.
# The batch script itself runs on the first allocated node. The srun commands
# create new job steps within the job's resource allocation.

echo "Starting Dask scheduler..."
srun -N 1 -n 1 dask-scheduler --scheduler-file $HOME/scheduler.json &

# Wait a few seconds for the scheduler to start and write its connection file
sleep 4

echo "Starting Dask workers..."
for((i=2; i<=$SLURM_NNODES; i++))
do 
   # This launches one worker as a separate job step. 
   # Since we have 7 nodes and 7 tasks total, this loop will run 6 times,
   # starting one worker on each of the remaining 6 nodes.
   echo "Starting worker on node $i..."
   srun -N 1 -n 1 dask-worker --scheduler-file $HOME/scheduler.json --nthreads 1 --nprocs 36 &
done

# Run the main python script which connects to the dask cluster.
# The job will terminate once this script is complete, and Slurm will clean up
# the backgrounded scheduler and worker processes.
python crsim_multidop_testing.py $HOME/scheduler.json

issues: The dask-worker arguments `--nthreads 1 --nprocs 36` are likely incorrect for the resource allocation. The intention is probably to have one worker process utilizing 36 threads, which would be specified with `--nprocs 1 --nthreads 36`. The current configuration will start 36 separate single-threaded worker processes on each node, which may lead to excessive memory overhead and is likely not the intended parallelism model.

The worker startup loop `for((i=2; i<=$SLURM_NNODES; i++))` is not robust. It assumes a sequential, numeric naming convention for nodes (e.g., node2, node3) which is not guaranteed across all clusters. A better practice is to parse the `$SLURM_JOB_NODELIST` environment variable to get the actual hostnames of the allocated nodes.

The `srun` command inside the loop does not explicitly target a specific node for each worker. While Slurm will distribute the single-task job steps among the available nodes in the allocation, it is better practice to explicitly assign workers to specific nodes from the nodelist for clarity and guaranteed distribution.

The environment variable `OMP_NUM_THREADS` is set to `$SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE`. It is more precise to use `$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK`, as this directly reflects the resources allocated to the task by the `--cpus-per-task=36` directive.

#!/bin/bash -l
#SBATCH -N 7        
#SBATCH --time=5:00:00   
#SBATCH --job-name=dask_cluster
#SBATCH -n 7
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=36

# Environment variables
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=$CPUS_ON_NODE
export MPLBACKEND="agg"
export LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8
export LANG=en_US.UTF-8
 
# Write ~/scheduler.json file in home directory
# connect with
# >>> from dask.distributed import Client
# >>> client = Client(scheduler_file='~/scheduler.json')

# Start scheduler on first process, workers on all others
echo $SLURM_PROCID
srun -N 1 -n1 dask-scheduler --scheduler-file $HOME/scheduler.json &
sleep 4
for((i=2; i<=$SLURM_NNODES; i++))
do 
   echo "Starting worker..." $i
   srun -N1 -n1 dask-worker --scheduler-file $HOME/scheduler.json --nthreads 1 --nprocs 36 &
done

python crsim_multidop_testing.py /home/rjackson/scheduler.json
